text: dsh-orchestrator 为 DSH web 增加 agent 与任务编排侧栏，并注册 orch_* 工具。用户可查看、创建、分叉和提示聊天，也能创建命令、抓取、HTTP 或 agent 任务并跟踪状态；任务支持本机、SSH 与 HTTP runner。适合需要集中管理多个 DSH 会话和任务的用户。需安装 dsh-better-sidebar；机器 API 可配置 DSH_ORCHESTRATOR_SECRET。

dsh-orchestrator adds agent and task controls to DSH web through a sidebar and orch_* tools. Users manage chats, start agents, create command, scrape, HTTP, or agent tasks, and use local, SSH, or HTTP runners. It requires dsh-better-sidebar; configure DSH_ORCHESTRATOR_SECRET for the machine API.
我想从一个侧栏查看并管理正在运行和已经休眠的 agent 聊天。
能不能一次开多个 agent 会话，分别分配不同任务？
我需要在 DSH 里创建网页抓取或 HTTP 请求任务，并跟踪执行状态。
dsh-orchestrator 的功能「Agent 会话编排」：在侧栏查看会话，并通过工具创建、分叉、提示或取消聊天；可批量启动多个会话并在列表中查看状态。
dsh-orchestrator 的功能「跟踪自动化任务」：创建命令、抓取、HTTP 或 agent 任务，在侧栏查看任务状态与输出；任务可以指定本机、SSH 或 HTTP runner。
dsh-orchestrator 使用机器 API 时需要配置 DSH_ORCHESTRATOR_SECRET 环境变量或设置页中的 API secret；未配置时该密钥保护的 API 请求无法使用。

**Agent swarm + task orchestration for DeepSeek Harness (DSH).**

A plugin that adds an **Orchestrate** tab to dsh-better-sidebar, like the built-in Background Tasks view, but broader:
section: restart dsh web, then open the Orchestrate tab

text:
@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · restart dsh web, then open the Orchestrate tab：- **Agents**: create, list, prompt, **fork** (split a conversation), fan-out and cancel agent chats, with a **chat-style** transcript drawer. Sessions address all of it through 14 `orch_*` tools.
- **Tasks**: tracked, status-updated work of four kinds: `command` (shell on any runner), `scrape` (deterministic multi-URL extraction, no model in the loop), `http` (endpoint calls), `agent` (a spawned chat whose answer is the task output).
- **Runners**: where commands execute: this host, ssh targets, or remote **tool servers** (any other host running this plugin). Explicit selection or the configured default.
- **Providers**: external integrations rendered as status cards, including an optional HPC allocation card and any JSON status endpoint.
- **Remote API**: a secret-protected machine API: prompt chats, spawn agents, create tasks, and serve the tool-server contract so OTHER hosts can run work here.
section: restart dsh web, then open the Orchestrate tab

text:
@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · restart dsh web, then open the Orchestrate tab：Everything is **settings-driven**: runners, providers, presets, limits and the API secret live in Settings → Orchestrator (or the cordis config row). Nothing is hardcoded, no hosts, no commands, no credentials in the code.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · Install：Requires DSH >= 0.1.1-rc.1, Node >= 22.5, the `web` profile, and dsh-better-sidebar (the tab host).

Install from npm: `dsh plugin --profile web add @lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator`, or from GitHub: `dsh plugin --profile web add github:lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator`.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator

@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · or from GitHub: dsh plugin --profile web add github:lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator：```

The package declares `dsh.bundle`, so `dsh plugin add` lists it in `dsh.profile.bundles`. From a checkout instead:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator
dsh plugin --profile web add link:$PWD/dsh-orchestrator
```

`lib/` is committed, so no build step is needed. Then **restart dsh-web** (the client half mounts live after a browser refresh; the host half, tools, settings namespace, API route, needs the restart). Full steps are in cordis.patch.yml.
section: or from GitHub: dsh plugin --profile web add github:lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator

text:
@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · The tab：| Section | What it shows / does |
|---|---|
| **agents** | every chat (live + cold) with title, running state, recency; quick **prompt**, **stop**, **chat** drawer (transcript + send box + fork + cancel); **+ new agent** spawn form with fan-out |
| **tasks** | every task with status, runner, live output (auto-polling while running), cancel; **+ new task** form for all four types |
| **runners** | execution targets with health probes |
| **providers** | integration cards, an hpc provider shows the allocation headline, queue, collector health and staged proposals |
| **api** | machine-API secret management + ready-made curl examples + the tool-server contract |
@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · The tab：A badge on the tab counts active work (running agents + running tasks).
@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · The agent tools：Sessions get these tools (registered through the standard `ctx.tools` seam, they behave like any core tool):

@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · The agent tools：| tool | what it does |
|---|---|
| `orch_status` | one-screen overview: agents, tasks by status, runners, providers |
| `orch_agents_list` | list chats (live/cold, titles, running flags), with search |
| `orch_agent_status` | one chat: running state + last user/assistant text |
| `orch_agent_prompt` | deliver a message into a chat (id, unique prefix, or exact title); cold chats resume |
| `orch_agent_spawn` | create chat(s), optionally with a first prompt; `count` fans out with `{i}` interpolation, **how you split work across agents** |
| `orch_agent_fork` | **split a conversation**: fork a chat's completed-turn history into a new session, then prompt the fork |
| `orch_agent_cancel` | cancel a chat's active turn (queued work is kept) |
| `orch_task_create` | create + run a task (see below) |
| `orch_task_list` / `orch_task_status` / `orch_task_output` | list / inspect / read tasks |
| `orch_task_cancel` | cancel a task (kills the runner process or cancels the agent turn) |
| `orch_runners` | runner inventory + health probes |
| `orch_providers` | provider status cards (for example an HPC allocation) |

@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · Task types：| type | spec fields | output |
|---|---|---|
| `command` | `command`, `cwd`, `runner`, `timeoutMs` | stdout + stderr, capped |
| `scrape` | `urls[]`, `extract` (text/html/json), `selector` (tag/.class/#id/[attr]), `attribute`, `pattern` (regex) | JSON rows: per-URL status + extracted data |
| `http` | `url`, `method`, `body`, `headers`, `expectStatus`, `timeoutMs` | response body, capped |
| `agent` | `prompt`, `count` (fan-out), `forkOf` (split an existing chat), `promptExisting` (drive an existing chat), `preset`, `cwd` | the chat itself, live status while it works, the assistant answer when it settles |

@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · Task types：All tasks: global concurrency cap with queueing, cancellation, durable history with pruning, and an audit event log. Tasks also mirror (best-effort) into `ctx.jobs` so they appear in the built-in Background Tasks surface.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · Task types：**Live output**: command tasks stream stdout/stderr into the task record as it arrives (the tab's output panel and `orch_task_output` show progress while the command runs, not just the final result); scrape tasks log per-URL progress lines (`[2/5] https://… -> 200`) before the structured JSON replaces them at settlement.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · Task types：After mounting (restart), verify the host with `bash scripts/verify-host.sh [port] [secret]`: health, dashboard shape, the trust fence, the CSRF gate, and (with the secret) a machine probe round trip.
@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · Runners: where work executes：Selection: explicit `runner` id, else the configured default, else round-robin across enabled runners.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · Providers: integrations：- **hpc** (optional): an adapter for an HPC allocation status service you run yourself (a GPU-hour grant, a cluster quota). It reads `{url}/health` and `{url}/state`; the contract is below. Leave it out if you have no such service.
- **http**: any JSON status endpoint; `ok`/`health`/`status`/`headline` keys are highlighted when present, everything else renders as fields. Optional `secretEnv` for a bearer token read at call time.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · Providers: integrations：Add your own control planes (pods, orchestrators, dashboards) as http providers; add your remote boxes as ssh or http runners. The plugin has **zero** knowledge of any specific host.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · The machine API：Protected by a secret (`DSH_ORCHESTRATOR_SECRET` env or Settings), constant-time compared, rate-limited per IP, **failing closed** when no secret is configured. Present it as `x-orchestrator-secret: <secret>` or `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`.

```sh

@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · prompt any chat (id, unique prefix, or exact title), cold chats resume：curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3080/dsh-orchestrator/api/remote/prompt \\
  -H "content-type: application/json" \\
  -H "x-orchestrator-secret: $DSH_ORCHESTRATOR_SECRET" \\
  -d '{"chat":"Research","message":"status report?"}'
section: prompt any chat (id, unique prefix, or exact title), cold chats resume

text:
@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · spawn an agent：curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3080/dsh-orchestrator/api/remote/agents/create \\
  -H "content-type: application/json" \\
  -H "x-orchestrator-secret: $DSH_ORCHESTRATOR_SECRET" \\
  -d '{"title":"nightly-research","prompt":"summarize todays papers","count":3}'

@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · run work on this host from anywhere (the tool-server contract)：curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3080/dsh-orchestrator/api/remote/run \\
  -H "content-type: application/json" \\
  -H "x-orchestrator-secret: $DSH_ORCHESTRATOR_SECRET" \\
  -d '{"kind":"command","spec":{"command":"uptime"},"timeoutMs":30000}'
section: run work on this host from anywhere (the tool-server contract)

text:
@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · -> {"ok":true,"status":"completed","output":"..."}：```

Reads (`/status`, `/agents`, `/tasks`, `/providers`, `/runners`, `/settings`) also answer to the secret. Browser reads are trust-fenced (loopback + Host authority); browser mutations additionally require the same-origin CSRF header set and the harness session cookie (see Security).

@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · Settings reference：Where the values live depends on the DSH line (lib/dual-settings.js picks it by capability): on DSH 0.1.5 they are the registered namespace `dsh-orchestrator` in `settings.yaml`; on DSH 0.2.x they are the `dsh-orchestrator` row of the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (every field live except `stateDir`), imported once from `settings.yaml.imported` while the row is still empty. `api.secret` is a secret field and is redacted on every read.
@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · Settings reference：Everything lives under the `dsh-orchestrator` settings namespace (Settings → Orchestrator) or the cordis config row. Highlights:

@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · Settings reference：| key | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | true | master switch |
| `api.secret` / env `DSH_ORCHESTRATOR_SECRET` |, | machine API secret (env wins; never echoed back) |
| `api.rateLimitPerMinute` | 60 | per-IP machine call budget |
| `agents.spawnMax` | 8 | fan-out cap per spawn |
| `agents.defaultPreset` / `agents.defaultCwd` |, | defaults for new chats |
| `tasks.maxConcurrent` | 4 | engine-wide live task cap |
| `tasks.defaultRunner` | local | runner for unqualified tasks |
| `tasks.allowCommandTasks` | true | can command tasks run at all |
| `tasks.allowRemoteRunners` | true | may tasks leave this host |
| `tasks.historyKeep` | 400 | finished tasks kept |
| `mirrorJobs` | true | mirror tasks into ctx.jobs (Background Tasks tab) |
| `runners[]` | local only | execution targets, see above |
| `providers[]` |, | integrations, see above |
| `trustedHosts[]` |, | extra Host authorities for the public edge |
@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · Kill switches：```sh

@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · ~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml：- id: dsh-orchestrator
  disabled: true

@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · runtime, no restart:：DSH_ORCHESTRATOR_DISABLE=1   # in the dsh-web environment
```

@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · Development：```sh
npm run check   # node --check every file
npm install     # devDependencies: esbuild, jsdom, react, react-dom
npm run build   # bundle src/client.jsx -> lib/client.js (esbuild, or ESBUILD_MAIN)
npm test        # host-half tests, lossless JSON checks, client render test, dual-settings tests

The client test needs jsdom and react from the devDependencies (or a package directory named by `DSH_TEST_REQUIRE_SEED`); without them it skips.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator README · Status：0.1.1: used daily on a real deployment. MIT license, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Issues and PRs welcome.
